title: gcmc params.json
description: Input template for a GCMC run or sweep. Pass to `python -m gcmc run` for one run, or to `python -m gcmc.launcher` for a sweep. For sweeps, set ensemble.mu, sampler.trial_density, and/or sampler.trial_box_side to a LIST; the launcher takes the Cartesian product (two lists = a heatmap). Every other field stays scalar. Ensembles: muVT (grand canonical), NVT (canonical: fixed N, and with a species file fixed counts PER SPECIES), semigrand (fixed total N, free composition), QA (quenched-annealed fluid in a frozen matrix; set ensemble.type='QA' and run.matrix_config). Any key beginning with an underscore is ignored by the validator, so a params file can carry its own explanation; every examples/*.json uses "_comment" for that.

main.description: hard_core: athermal exclusion. lennard_jones: requires T.

T.description: Reduced temperature T*; required iff main == lennard_jones, forbidden otherwise.

tail.description: LJ long-range tail correction; lennard_jones only.

species_file.description: Path to a schema-2 reduced species yaml (ff/species_*.yaml). Present selects typed multi-species mode: the file owns sigma, epsilon, lambda, p_trial, symbol, k_ij, rc, core_floor.c and the auxiliary, so run.radius, run.lower_cutoff, run.upper_cutoff and the auxiliary block are forbidden. Requires main == lennard_jones.

auxiliary.description: OPTIONAL. Omit for no auxiliary (pure main potential). 'pmf' adds a tabulated g3 selection bias. 'short_range' is dual-cutoff CBMC: the same Lennard-Jones truncated at auxiliary.cutoff is used to propose and select, and the mismatch against run.upper_cutoff is divided back out in the acceptance. Both leave the sampled ensemble unchanged; they only change which moves get proposed.

g3_csv.description: Path to the g3 table; required in 3D.

min_g3.description: 3D pmf only; OPTIONAL. The floor applied to the tabulated g3(r, cos theta), both to the grid before interpolation and to the interpolated value. Omit for the historical default 1/sampler.trials, which moves whenever the trial count moves; pin it (e.g. 0.03) to make the selection bias independent of k. Forbidden in 2D, where the analytic hard-disk g(r) has no floor, and with auxiliary.type='short_range', which has no table.

eta.description: 2D analytic g(r) packing fraction (2D pmf only).

cutoff.description: short_range only, and required for it: the radius the proposal and the clique sum are evaluated at, e.g. 1.5. Must satisfy run.lower_cutoff < cutoff <= run.upper_cutoff. The PHYSICS cutoff is always run.upper_cutoff and is not changed by this key; cutoff == run.upper_cutoff is legal and is the exact no-op control. Supported for sampler.type='channel' with potential.main='lennard_jones' in 3D bulk.

gamma.description: pmf only; OPTIONAL. The selection-bias exponent per Rosenbluth level, in place of the fitted schedule in _GAMMA_AUX_2D / _GAMMA_AUX_3D. A SCALAR applies at every level (0.1 is the nine-vector of 0.1); an ARRAY of 1 to 9 values gives the first levels and leaves the rest at 0, so [0.29, 0.10, 0.03] biases the first three placements of a move and leaves deeper ones unbiased. Padding with zero rather than repeating the last value follows the fitted table, whose levels 7 to 9 are already 0, and is the safe direction: a missing entry costs efficiency while an extrapolated one applies a bias nobody chose at a depth nobody measured. Both dimensions read it, the 2D analytic hard-disk g(r) and the 3D tabulated g3 alike. Identity-bearing, since two exponents select differently; absent means the fitted schedule and keeps every pre-existing run id. Refused on auxiliary.type='short_range', which has no exponent. SWEEPABLE: to the launcher the outer list is always the sweep and each element is one arm, a scalar or an array, so [0.0, 0.05, 0.1] is three arms and [[0.29,0.10,0.03]] is one arm holding that array. A bare flat list is therefore a sweep of scalars; wrap an array to pin it. A nested list reaching a single run is refused by name, because it means the sweep was never expanded.

g3_r_cut.description: 3D pmf only; OPTIONAL. A neighbour further than this radius contributes NOTHING to the selection bias, i.e. its g3 factor is 1. Absent means every neighbour inside run.upper_cutoff contributes, which is what every run before this key did. WHY: the bias is a product over neighbours, so every pair multiplies in whether or not it carries information, and on data/g3_analysis_data.csv the angular structure dies out by r = 1.9 -- the spread of log g3 over cos theta falls from 2.8 at contact to 0.26 by r = 1.975, and pairs beyond r = 1.8 hold about 4% of the total variance while being roughly two thirds of the pairs. Those pairs cost time and make the bias depend on how MANY neighbours a trial has rather than on where it sits. Ranked offline with scripts/aux_variants.py, cutting at 1.8 to 1.9 raised the rank correlation between the bias and the room a choice leaves for the molecules still to be placed, at unchanged variance; cutting at 1.6 or below lowered it, so there is a real optimum and it should be measured on the configuration rather than assumed. Identity-bearing, like min_g3 and gamma: it cannot move an equilibrium average, because the bias is divided back out of the acceptance, and it changes which trial is selected. Refused in 2D, where the auxiliary is the analytic hard-disk g(r) with no neighbour product to truncate, and at or below contact, where every pair would be dropped and the bias would be identically 1 while still paying for the lookup.

type.description: metropolis: single-particle. rosenbluth/branch: cavity-biased insertion (depth 0-3). channel: oriented-cuboid transfer-matrix sweep (3D, serial, depth >= 1 unless full_repacking), with channel_length either a number (fixed rod) or "full" (this move's chord less a frozen gap, ladder engines only). reweight: 2D hexatic. The wall-to-wall rod that closed on itself through the periodic boundary was a separate sampler until 2026-10; it had no separable exterior, so no ladder engine could run it, and channel_length = "full" replaced it with the same chord held open by a frozen gap.

oneOf.description: fixed-length rod: the long axis of the oriented trial cuboid. Must satisfy the periodic guard sqrt(channel_length^2 + 2*channel_width^2) <= box - cutoff, so trial distances never wrap.

full-span rod with a frozen gap: the body is an oriented cuboid whose LENGTH comes from the drawn orientation -- the furthest that direction runs before passing within the interaction range of its own periodic image, capped at the box body diagonal. What is left of the torus is the frozen gap, which is why the body stays an OPEN rod and is swept by the ordinary open-rod transfer matrix. The length does not depend on where the body sits, which is what lets the Metropolis removal leg offset it around an anchor; every dynamics accepts it. Requires trial_density; sampler.trials is rejected because the length, hence the trial count, varies per move.

channel_length.description: Rod length for sampler.type = "channel", in reduced units: a positive number for a fixed-length oriented cuboid, or "full" for the full-span rod with a frozen gap. The spellings that used to select the rod that closed on itself ("cyclic", "box", "full_box", "span") are refused: that rod is gone, and "full" is the same chord with a gap in it. Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width.

channel_width.description: channel only: side of the square cross-section, required in [sigma, 2 sigma]. The trial cuboid volume is channel_length * channel_width^2. Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width.

trials.description: Fixed trial count per cavity. Mutually exclusive with trial_density; forbidden for metropolis. Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width.

trial_density.description: Trial count set by density x trial-box span. Forbidden for metropolis. SWEEPABLE: a list builds one run per value. Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width.

trial_box_side.description: rosenbluth/branch only: full side of the square trial box (twice the legacy cavity radius). Forbidden for metropolis and rejected for channel (which uses channel_length/channel_width with trial_density). SWEEPABLE: a list builds one run per value (pair with trial_density for a heatmap). Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width.

sampler.description: Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width. A CANONICAL run (ensemble.type='NVT' with a species file) proposes translations and pair identity exchanges and runs no trial cloud, so its whole sampler block is {"type": "metropolis"}.

type.description: The DYNAMICS axis, which is not the same axis as sampler.type. `sampler.type` says how a trial cloud is PROPOSED; `engine` says what is then done with it. metropolis_dynamics (the default, and what an absent key means -- that is the backward-compatibility contract) is accept/reject dynamics: everything shipped before this key existed. glauber_dynamics computes the exact conditional distribution of a window's whole guest content and draws from it, so its exchange path has no acceptance test: dN = k_new - k_in may take any sign and any magnitude, and add/remove/repack cease to be separate move types. Same muVT ensemble, same z, same U -- a different transition kernel. Both ladder dynamics REQUIRE sampler.type='channel' with depth >= 1; refused with metropolis, rosenbluth, branch, reweight. Refuses the pmf and short-range auxiliaries: both are selection biases divided back out in an acceptance ratio, and this engine has none. Caps the trial density at 20 trials per eviction window (rc) of channel length on the LJ path. Adding this key moves every run id, by decision: resuming a pre-engine run directory is not supported. Serial only. Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type and engine; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side and engine; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length, channel_width and kmax_margin. suwa_todo_dynamics is the THIRD dynamics and the sibling of glauber_dynamics, not a variant of it: it builds the same window, the same pool and the same exact occupancy ladder, and then draws k from that ladder by the Suwa-Todo geometric allocation (PRL 105, 120603 (2010)) conditioned on the incoming occupancy, rather than categorically. glauber_dynamics is a heat bath and returns the incoming occupancy with probability P(k_in); the allocation is the pi-invariant kernel that MINIMISES that rate, and it achieves it by giving up detailed balance and keeping only global balance. Same muVT ensemble, same z, same U, same stationary distribution, so every physics gate written for glauber_dynamics applies verbatim. It takes exactly the keys glauber_dynamics takes, has the same refusals (sampler.type='channel', depth >= 1, no pmf or short-range auxiliary, serial only, the trials-per-eviction-window cap on the LJ path), and adds none of its own. The gain is bounded: the rate at which k changes improves by at most a factor 2 over the heat bath and by much less for a ladder concentrated on one rung, so the ratio is read off the log's ladder_unchanged column rather than assumed.

depth.description: Cavity recursion depth; forbidden for metropolis. Any depth >= 0 is supported, serially and in parallel -- the cap of 3 that stood here until 2026-08 was a stale claim, not a constraint, and it REJECTED runs the engine handles. Mutually exclusive with full_repacking. Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width.

full_repacking.description: XOR alternative to depth: repack the whole cavity each exchange, removing every sphere found and inserting one more (add), one fewer (remove), or the same count (repack). Ignores depth; do not give both. Cavity samplers only (not metropolis). Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length and channel_width.

kmax_margin.description: The ladder dynamics (glauber_dynamics, suwa_todo_dynamics) only, and its ONLY new tunable: how far above the body's geometric packing bound the occupancy ladder is truncated. kmax = min(M, ceil(packing_bound(body)) + kmax_margin) and M = round(trial_density * channel_length * channel_width^(dim-1)); both are derived, so neither appears here. The bound is a rigorous over-estimate, so 0 is the honest default and a positive margin only widens the transfer matrix. Refused under engine=metropolis_dynamics, which has no ladder. Only the samplers that READ a key may state it; any other sampler refuses it by name rather than ignoring it. Readers: metropolis takes no key but type and engine; rosenbluth/branch/reweight take depth, full_repacking, trials, trial_density, trial_box_side and engine; channel takes those minus trial_box_side plus channel_length, channel_width and kmax_margin.

mu.description: Chemical potential mu* (TOTAL: activity z = exp(beta*mu)). REQUIRED for muVT and QA; forbidden for NVT. QA may use mu < 0. SWEEPABLE: a list builds one run per value. With a target, mu is an OPTIONAL starting seed (default: the ideal-gas guess ln(rho_target)). In typed mode this is a map {species: number}, one entry per species, and z_s = exp(beta*mu_s)/lambda_s**dim.

box.description: Box side. A number gives a cubic box (volume = box^dimension). A FLAT list of one length per axis (Lx, Ly[, Lz]) gives a single orthorhombic box (volume = product of the sides); an isotropic list collapses to the scalar. A NESTED list (list of box-specs) is SWEEPABLE: the launcher runs one job per element, each a number (cubic) or per-axis list (orthorhombic), e.g. [[45,45,56],[50,50,60]]. Supported by every sampler and the parallel decomposition; only a confined pore requires a scalar box.

type.description: muVT: grand canonical (give mu). NVT: CANONICAL -- give exactly one of N or packing_fraction and no mu. With a species file NVT means every species count is fixed, not just the total: the composition is the one in run.initial_config (which is then required), the move set becomes translation plus a pair identity exchange, and two coexisting phases are the equilibrium rather than a transient. semigrand: SEMI-GRAND -- total N fixed, composition FREE under the activity ratio. Species file required, plus exactly one state-point route (mu/fugacity/z) whose RATIO does the work; give N or packing_fraction as in NVT. This is what typed NVT used to mean, and it was renamed because the two are different ensembles and one name for both had already produced three cluster campaigns that dissolved into a single phase. QA: quenched-annealed = muVT in a frozen matrix (give mu AND run.matrix_config; mu may be < 0 for the dilute isotherm). confined: grand canonical in a hard slit or cylinder pore (give mu and ensemble.pore; 3D only; no matrix).

pore.description: confined only: a hard wall inside the periodic box. slit walls sit at z=0 and z=H; a cylinder of radius R runs along z through the centre. Every gap must admit a whole sphere (2*radius).

H.description: slit gap in z; must exceed the diameter and stay below box - diameter.

R.description: cylinder radius; 2R must exceed the diameter and stay below box - diameter.

N.description: NVT and semigrand only: exact particle count, held fixed. SWEEPABLE. Mutually exclusive with packing_fraction.

packing_fraction.description: NVT only: converted to nearest integer N = round(eta * V / v_particle), then held exactly. SWEEPABLE.

target_eta.description: muVT target control: drive mu until the running-mean packing fraction reaches this value. Mutually exclusive with mu(sweep) and the other targets. SWEEPABLE: a list runs one job per value (launch with gcmc.launcher). When swept against a matrix FOLDER, each value is paired by index with one realization matrix.

target_density.description: muVT target control: drive mu until the running-mean reduced density rho*=N/V reaches this value. SWEEPABLE: a list runs one job per value (launch with gcmc.launcher). When swept against a matrix FOLDER, each value is paired by index with one realization matrix.

target_N.description: muVT target control: drive mu until the running-mean particle count <N> reaches this value. SWEEPABLE: a list runs one job per value (launch with gcmc.launcher). When swept against a matrix FOLDER, each value is paired by index with one realization matrix.

fugacity.description: Typed mode only: per-species fugacity map; z_s = beta*f_s, and lambda is not consulted. Mutually exclusive with mu and z.

z.description: Typed mode only: per-species activity map, used directly. Mutually exclusive with mu and fugacity.

kind.description: single: one serial chain (1 core). parallel: cell-decomposed (uses n_workers cores).

n_cell.description: PARALLEL, RECOMMENDED FORM. Number of cells the box is cut into. One cell is one core, so this IS the core count for the run and no core count is stated separately. An integer is factored across the axes to give the most cubic cells possible; a per-axis list [nx, ny, nz] is honoured verbatim. Everything else (per-axis cell lengths, buffer) is derived, so cell_length / buffer / x_spacing / y_spacing must NOT be given alongside it. Either submit n_cell, or state the full geometry yourself; there is nothing in between. A count the box cannot take is an error listing the nearest usable counts, never a silent reduction to fewer cells than cores.

n_cores.description: Launcher only: the TOTAL core budget for a sweep (= --cores N). The launcher refuses to start if (sweep combinations) x (cores per run) exceeds it, where cores-per-run is the cell count for a parallel run and 1 for a serial one. Not accepted on a parallel base, where the per-run core count is the cell count and cannot be restated.

cell_length.description: MANUAL parallel geometry. Per-cell side, scalar or per-axis list. REQUIRED together with buffer when run.n_cell is absent (there is no default: the historical 30 was unusable for any box <= 32). Must not be given alongside run.n_cell. The cell count then falls out as floor(box / (cell_length + buffer)) per axis.

buffer.description: MANUAL parallel geometry. Width of the frozen border ring; REQUIRED together with cell_length when run.n_cell is absent. Must be >= the interaction range (rc for LJ, 2*radius for hard core) so a border ring holds every molecule that can interact with a live one. In n_cell mode this is derived as exactly the interaction range, which makes the cells as large as the physics allows.

traj_every.description: Trajectory saving. 0 (default) = save ONLY the last frame (one overwritten snapshot in trajectory.extxyz). N >= 1 = append every N-th window's configuration to a growing trajectory (N=1 saves every window). Use traj_every=1 for QA RDF runs, which need every frame. On resume, an append-mode trajectory is trimmed to the checkpoint step so frames are never duplicated.

initial_config.description: Starting configuration; omit to start fresh (bulk muVT starts empty, NVT/QA/confined seed a valid start). Three forms. (0) The literal token "grid" (not a path): bootstrap from a periodic-commensurate lattice at a reasonable fluid packing fraction -- 0.35 in 3D, 0.45 in 2D -- instead of from an empty box, for when growing from N=0 is too slow. "grid:0.28" (or "grid=0.28") sets the packing fraction explicitly; a muVT target density (target_N / target_eta / target_density) is otherwise adopted as the target, and NVT ignores the density and places exactly N. Spacing always exceeds the contact distance, and sites that overlap a QA matrix or fall outside a confining pore are dropped, so the achieved density can be lower than asked (it is logged, and a gap above 15% is warned about). The remaining two forms are paths. (1) A path to a single file: extended-XYZ (atom-count line, a Lattice/Properties comment, then `species x y z` rows) or a bare `x y z` float table; the first line decides which. (2) A path to the equilibrated library directory, nested by system, temperature (LJ only) and box, e.g. lj/T_0.85/box_20/mu_0.0_lj_3d_box20.xyz or hard_disk_2d/box_200/mu_1.00_hard_2d_box_200.xyz. The per-run file is found by matching chemical potential, box, dimension and (for LJ) temperature, tolerant of the differing decimal and box_<L> vs box<L> filename styles. A run raises if nothing matches (it lists what is present) or if several match (it lists the candidates). SWEEPABLE: a list builds one run per start, which is how a state point is shown to have converged (arms begun from different configurations must meet). The start is NOT identity-bearing -- a warm start changes how fast a chain reaches equilibrium, not which equilibrium -- so the arms share a run id and are kept in separate directories by the sweep label alone, which is built from as much of each path as it takes to tell them apart.

radius.description: Particle radius (diameter = 2 x radius = LJ sigma).

matrix_config.description: REQUIRED iff ensemble.type='QA'; forbidden otherwise. Absolute path to the frozen matrix configuration (an NVT checkpoint.npz, an extended-XYZ .xyz/.extxyz, or a plain 'x y z' file). The fluid cannot overlap these obstacles, which are never inserted/deleted/moved/counted. The matrix content is folded into the run-id hash (distinct realizations -> distinct dirs) and snapshotted into the run directory as matrix.npz, so a resume is self-contained even if the source file moves. QA supports hard_core or LJ+branch, sampler rosenbluth/branch, and run.kind='single' only. May also be a FOLDER of realizations (subdirs each with trajectory.extxyz or checkpoint.npz, or a flat folder of *.xyz/*.extxyz/*.npz): then a list target sweep pairs each swept value with one matrix by sorted index (16 targets -> 16 matrices -> 16 runs). The last frame of each trajectory is used. A folder is only valid via gcmc.launcher, not a single `gcmc run`.

control_gain.description: Robbins-Monro gain for muVT target control: mu += gain/(1+win/gain_tau) * (ln N_target - ln <N>) per window.

control_gain_tau.description: Decay scale (in windows) of the target-control gain; larger = slower decay, more aggressive late correction.

control_window.description: Number of windows in the running mean of N that the target controller steers (and reports as avgN).

sweep_label.description: Written BY gcmc.launcher into each expanded run, naming the swept axes and their values (e.g. 'mu2.0_seed3'); it names the run directory and is not normally set by hand. It is declared here because run.additionalProperties is false, so without it every launcher-expanded config would fail validation against this schema.

_comment.description: Free text, ignored by the validator. Any underscore-prefixed key is ignored, at the top level and inside every section, so the reason for a run can live in the run.
